## What to Consider

Bento has become a popular choice for creators who want a design-forward, card-based link hub that feels more like a personal homepage than a basic “link in bio.” The alternatives split into distinct camps: mainstream, no-fuss hubs like Linktree that emphasize reliability and built-in click analytics; lightweight one-page builders like Carrd for shipping simple landing pages fast at a strong price-to-power ratio; and more feature-led options like Hopp by Wix, which stands out with search to help visitors find older content. If you want more than links, tools like Zaap bundle list-building newsletters and a small shop, while IndiePage caters to indie makers who want a founder/startup portfolio with community discovery. Carrd leans into being a true one-page website builder, not just a link list, which makes it a compelling alternative to Bento when you need a broader landing-page canvas. It’s designed for shipping lightweight pages fast, from personal profiles to product waitlists.

Compared with Bento’s card-based “profile hub” feel, Carrd offers more flexibility for building a small standalone site: structured sections, polished templates, and the ability to publish a page that feels like a mini landing site rather than a bio directory. It’s especially strong when the goal is a focused message and a single conversion path.

results.title: Best Bento.me Alternatives for Creators in 2026
results.content:
### What happened to Bento.me?

Bento.me shut down in early 2026. If your page lived there, rebuild it on another platform and update the link in your social profiles.

### What is the closest alternative to Bento.me?

Avely, if you want the visual, modular grid back. Taap.bio is the other close call, especially if you want an automated Bento migration.

### Can I use a Bento alternative as a portfolio?

Yes, as long as the tool supports images, media, text, and flexible layouts, not just link buttons. Add a clear contact or booking action and you’re set.

### Should I use a custom domain for my creator page?

Worth it once the page represents your professional identity. You get a stable URL that stays yours even if you switch tools later.

## Sources and further reading [...] Taplink leans toward forms, products, and small-business landing pages. Beacons bundles a wider set of creator business tools.

Stan Store is its own category. Pick it when your page exists to sell: downloads, courses, coaching, memberships.

Later shines if you want your page to mirror your social feed and make individual posts clickable. The best alternative isn’t the one with the longest checklist. It’s the one whose main workflow matches yours.

## How to move off Bento without losing what worked

Don’t start by recreating every tile. Start with what each tile was for.

Most Bento pages picked up clutter over time: old experiments, inactive accounts, links that stopped pulling their weight. Moving is your excuse to cut all of it. Clean slate, better page.

1. 1 [...] It’s free to start. Paid plans add a custom domain, so your page lives at your own address.

### Best for

Designers, visual creators, freelancers, brands, and teams who want a page people explore, not a list they scan.

## 2–10. When another alternative fits you better

Taap.bio is aimed squarely at former Bento users, with one-click migration. If you want your links and widgets moved fast, without rethinking the page, that’s your shortcut.

Carrd gives you more design control. The catch: you make every design decision and wire up integrations yourself.

Milkshake keeps that flipping-through-cards feel, which is lovely if your audience lives on phones. Linktree and Lnk.Bio are the easy picks when you just want something familiar, fast.
